::: {.callout-note}
[`dvs history`](#dvs-history) is all that normal use requires. The rest of
this page is implementation detail.
:::

Every `init` and `add` is appended to `audit.log.jsonl` in the storage
directory. The log is append-only and newline-delimited JSON, with one operation
per line.

# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
options(width = 1000)
library(dvs)
library(fs)
library(here)
```

```{r}
source(here::here("R/mkdatasetfiles.R"))
```

```{r}
storage     <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_storage"))
new_project <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_project"))
dir.create(here::here(storage))
dir.create(here::here(new_project))
```

Run a sequence of dvs operations to populate the log:

```{r}
#| warning: false
setwd(here::here(new_project))
mkdatasetfiles(n_files = 3, size_mb = 2, prefix = "file_", dir = "data", show_progress = !nzchar(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH")))
dvs_init(here::here(storage))
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
setwd(here::here(new_project))
invisible(dvs_add("data/file_1.csv", message = "initial add of file 1"))
invisible(dvs_add("data/file_2.csv", message = "initial add of file 2"))
invisible(dvs_add("data/file_3.csv", message = "initial add of file 3"))
```

Restore a file with `get`. `get` does not append to the audit log; only `init`
and `add` are recorded.

```{r}
#| warning: false
setwd(here::here(new_project))
unlink("data/file_1.csv")
dvs_get("data/file_1.csv")
```

Modify `file_2.csv` and re-add:

```{r}
#| include: false
# The log records whole seconds. Keep the two adds of file_2 apart, so that
# dvs history orders them.
Sys.sleep(1.1)
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
setwd(here::here(new_project))
cat("99,0,0,0,0,0\n", file = "data/file_2.csv", append = TRUE)
invisible(dvs_add("data/file_2.csv", message = "updated file 2, added row 99"))
```

# dvs history

`dvs history` reads the log for you. Run it in the project folder with one or
more files. It lists every add of those files in one table, newest first: the
time in UTC, the user, the path, the first 12 characters of the BLAKE3 hash,
and the message.

```{r}
#| include: false
Sys.setenv(DVS_PROJECT = here::here(new_project))
```

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs history data/file_2.csv data/file_1.csv
```

- `user` is the account name of whoever ran the add, from the operating
  system. It is not the git identity.
- The log is in storage, not in git. So `dvs history` lists every add that
  reached this storage, also an add whose meta file was never committed or
  pushed. The version this checkout tracks is the hash in its meta file, which
  `dvs status --with-metadata` shows.
- It takes files, not folders. A folder is refused with exit code 2. The files
  need not be on disk. A file with no add in this storage prints `No history`.
- The log records whole seconds. Two adds in the same second can be listed in
  either order.

`--json` gives each entry as the log has it, with the full hash, and the time
as RFC 3339 UTC. Sort by `timestamp` rather than relying on the order of
`files`:

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs history --json data/file_2.csv |
  jq -r '.files | sort_by(.timestamp) | .[] | [.timestamp, .user, .action.add.file.hashes.blake3] | @tsv'
```

`dvs availability` says whether storage still holds a version. It takes full
hashes, not the 12 characters of the table. It prints `present` or `absent` for
each hash and exits 0 either way, so a script checks the word:

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs history --json data/file_2.csv |
  jq -r '.files[].action.add.file.hashes.blake3' |
  xargs dvs availability
```

R has no history function. The sections below read the log directly.

# Reading the log

The audit log is a newline-delimited JSON file (`audit.log.jsonl`) in the
storage directory. Each line is one operation:

```{r}
audit_path <- here::here(storage, "audit.log.jsonl")
```

Raw file, one JSON object per line:

```{r}
#| results: asis
lines <- readLines(audit_path)
cat("```json\n")
cat(lines, sep = "\n")
cat("\n```\n")
```

Same entries, pretty-printed:

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat("```json\n")
for (l in lines) {
  cat(jsonlite::toJSON(jsonlite::fromJSON(l, simplifyVector = FALSE), pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE))
  cat("\n")
}
cat("```\n")
```

# Parsing the log

Each entry has the shape:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "<uuid>",
  "timestamp":    <unix-seconds>,
  "user":         "<username>",
  "action":       { "<command>": { ... } }
}
```

The `action` field is a tagged union. The single key is the command name,
either `"init"` or `"add"` (`get` is not logged). Parse it with `purrr` and
`jsonlite`:

```{r}
#| warning: false
parse_entry <- function(line) {
  entry <- jsonlite::fromJSON(line)
  cmd   <- names(entry$action)[1]
  # init records settings and project_path, not a file, so it has no path.
  path  <- switch(cmd,
    add  = entry$action$add$file$path,
    init = NA_character_,
    NA_character_
  )
  list(
    operation_id = entry$operation_id,
    timestamp    = as.POSIXct(entry$timestamp, origin = "1970-01-01"),
    user         = entry$user,
    command      = cmd,
    path         = path
  )
}

audit_tbl <- readLines(audit_path) |>
  purrr::map(parse_entry) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

audit_tbl
```

# Querying the log

Operations by command type:

```{r}
dplyr::count(audit_tbl, command, sort = TRUE)
```

Files touched per operation (excluding `init`):

```{r}
#| warning: false
audit_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(path)) |>
  dplyr::select(timestamp, command, path) |>
  dplyr::arrange(timestamp)
```

How many times was each file touched?

```{r}
#| warning: false
audit_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(path)) |>
  dplyr::count(path, command, sort = TRUE)
```

# Cleanup

```{r}
unlink(here::here(new_project), recursive = TRUE)
unlink(here::here(storage),     recursive = TRUE)
```
